Operations.Value: Caelen possesses the System interface, which displays two distinct columns of advancement levels.
The System interface is private and cannot be seen or verified by others.
Caelen is currently in the void, suspended between lives.
Caelen's physical body was destroyed by gunfire, with wounds in his chest and thigh.
Caelen's past actions included lying to his mother about injuries and taking credit for Private Davis's tactical call.
Caelen was alive and physically present in a combat zone; Caelen is now dead and his consciousness is suspended in the void.
Caelen did not possess the System; Caelen now possesses the System and can perceive his advancement levels.
The void is a space defined by the absence of boundaries, characterized by soft, gray luminescence and a lack of physical laws such as gravity.
Souls in the void can perceive other souls as distant presences.
The System interface appears as translucent numbers in the periphery of the bearer's vision, consisting of two columns separated by a shimmering line.
Caelen is dead and currently in the void.
Caelen's physical body is destroyed.
Caelen's memories of his first life are fading and becoming emotionally distant.
Caelen is aware of his existence as a soul suspended in time.
Sergeant Miller is perceived by Caelen as having a personal hatred toward him.
Caelen took credit for Private Davis's tactical call.
Caelen died shielding The Mother from Sergeant Miller's gunfire.
The narrative has moved from the moment of Caelen's death to his consciousness in the void.
Caelen has perceived the System interface for the first time.
Caelen has begun the process of emotional processing and memory fading in the void.
The specific meaning and function of the two columns of numbers in the System interface are not explained to Caelen.
The duration of Caelen's stay in the void before his next return is not specified.
